title: Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
summary: Apple's new HomeView smart display ad depicts a chaotic morning routine with a family of five, departing from Apple's typical clean aesthetic. The commercial resonates particularly with parents of teenagers who see their own hectic mornings reflected on screen.
content:
Nothing like a little family togetherness in the morning. | Image: Apple	

Apple's ad introducing its new HomeView smart display is a little unusual. It's fast-paced and unruly, depicting a family of five as they rush through the morning routine. There's yelling and mess, misplaced keys and discarded eggshells. Apple's typical vibe is clean, simple, orderly; this commercial is chaos.
But the spot has parents - those with teen children in particular - feeling seen.

I'll admit that it stressed me out the first time I watched it, too. Mornings getting my five-year-old out the door are a special breed of chaos, and usually culminate in us playing whatever ad-libbed game will get him to put his shoes on. But it's not  …

title: The Nothing Headphone A are half off for the first time
summary: The Nothing Headphone A over-ear headphones are available at their lowest price of $97.52 when bundled with a Charli XCX album on Amazon, representing a 33 percent discount.
content:
The Headphone A keep the shape and style of Nothing’s over-ear design, but with an opaque instead of transparent case. | Photo by John Higgins / The Verge	

One of the best deals we’ve seen today bundles together a great pair of headphones with a solid album. When you add the Nothing Headphone A in black or white and the CD version of the Charli XCX album Music, Fashion, Film to your Amazon cart, you’ll save 33 percent on your order, bringing the total down to $97.52. That’s lower than the best price we’ve seen for the headphones on their own, which retail for $199, and you get a free album to boot. The other colors also qualify for the discount, but have a higher starting price, so the discounted price will be higher as well.
Nothing Headphone A
Nothing’s second over-ear headphones may not offer everything found on the pricier Nothing Headphone 1, but you do get physical controls, good sound, and more than five days of battery life per charge. Their design is also a bit more discreet, for better or worse. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $136.79 $97.52 at Amazon (when bundled with album)

We reviewed the Nothing Headphone A when they launched earlier in 2026, and praised them for their physical controls, IP52 dust and water resistance rating, and excellent battery life. They have a more subtle design than other Nothing products, opting for an opaque housing instead of the translucent shells on other Nothing headphones.
Read our Nothing Headphone A review.

summary: Apple has launched the HomeView, a compact 7-inch smart display priced at $299 with Siri AI, video calling, and photo display in wall-mount or speaker-base configurations. The device's square design positions it as less imposing than competing smart displays.
content:
The HomeView is a smart speaker with a touchscreen display. It’s available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. | Image: Apple	

It's finally here: Apple's long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it's gorgeous. The HomeView puts a small, vibrant screen atop a speaker base for taking video calls, beautifully displaying photos, and providing information at a glance with Apple's Siri AI voice assistant. The device's square shape makes it feel less imposing than larger smart displays like Google's Nest Hub Max or Amazon's Echo Show 11, and I can see it fitting nicely on my kitchen counter - though it might be a hair too big for my bedside table.

title: Elgato takes on DJI with a tiny wireless mic for creators on the go
summary: Elgato has introduced the Wave Go, a $99.99 wireless microphone for mobile creators that competes with DJI's Mic Mini. The pea-sized device weighs only seven grams and offers broadcast-quality audio with noise cancellation.
content:
The Wave Go microphone is around the size of an AirPod. | Image: Elgato	

Elgato already dominates the market for hardware built for creators that use powerful desktop PCs, and it's now turning its attention to creators on the go with its first wireless microphone. The $99.99 Wave Go clips onto your clothes just like DJI's Mic Mini, with hands-free recording for vlogging and content creation.
The Wave Go is tiny, about the size of an AirPod, so it disappears on camera and only weighs seven grams. Despite the tiny size, Elgato is promising "broadcast-quality" audio, with a condenser capsule that supports EQ shift, auto gain, and noise cancellation.
